statement: Tim is 8 years old. His sister is 3 years younger than Tim. How old was his sister 2 years ago?

choices.misconception: I found how old his sister is now and stopped there.
I found how old Tim was 2 years ago instead of his sister.
I added 2 years instead of going back 2 years.
I made his sister 3 years older than Tim instead of younger, then went back 2 years.

hints: Who does the question ask about, and when?
Underline what the question wants: the sister, and her age in the past. First find her age now, then go back in time.
His sister is 8 - 3 = 5 now. Two years ago she was 2 years younger than that.

solutions.reliable: Tim is 8 and his sister is 3 years younger, so she is 5 now. Two years ago she was 5 - 2 = 3. The idea to keep: before answering, check who and when the question asks about.

whyOnTest: Age questions ask about a particular person at a particular time, and most wrong answers answer a different person or time.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
